brief: A tight hyperreal portrait of a bay horse's muzzle on a frigid clear morning. Frost crusts the whiskers and eyelashes, and breath hangs as a pale veil. The coat is built from layered charcoal mass and soft coloured-pencil strokes in burnt umber and chestnut. Suspended in the air is a field of glittering diamond-dust crystals: tiny white pen sparks and needle-thin cross glints scattered through a pale cerulean-to-ice-grey atmosphere. The light is low and from behind, rimming every hair. The mood is crystalline, breath-held and very cold.

A boulder entirely encrusted with lichen, seen close and filling the frame. Rosettes grow within rosettes in self-similar crusts of chartreuse, sulphur yellow, slate blue-grey and rust orange. It is rendered almost entirely in dense pen stippling, millions of dots clustering into ever-smaller lobes as the eye zooms in. Fine pencil cracks in the rock thread between the colonies. There is no horizon and no focal point, only an endless coastline of edges. The effect is hypnotic, infinitely recursive and botanically exact.

An unknotted viridian silk necktie dropped on crumpled white hotel sheets, photographed-close. The duchess silk is crushed into sharp creases that flash from deep bottle green to almost white along every ridge. It is built from countless burnished layers of coloured pencil, so the surface looks lacquered. The sheets are rendered in cool grey pencil with soft shadows. The light is raking morning window light from one side. The crop is tight and diagonal. The feeling is the aftermath of a long night, sensual and rumpled.

A sleeping tabby cat rendered in hyperreal fur, every whisker and striped guard hair in fine coloured pencil. It lies on a quilt of flat, unshaded pattern in the Nabis manner: ochre checks, plum dots and olive sprigs. Behind it, wallpaper of a different flat pattern presses forward with no perspective at all. The patterns are laid as dense matte marker blocks with no gradation. The tension is the point: one fully modelled living body sinking into a decorative plane. The palette is muted and domestic, and the composition is cropped close and tilted.

A sheer sandstone canyon wall seen straight-on, its stepped ledges and serrated erosion terraces echoing Navajo stepped-diamond designs. Everything is built from tight horizontal strokes like packed weft. These run in pencil and marker in brick red, natural grey, charcoal black and undyed cream, with crisp stair-stepped boundaries between bands. Hyperreal detail lives inside each band: grain, desert varnish streaks and a tiny juniper clinging to a ledge. The light is flat midday. The piece is monumental, rhythmic and earthbound.

A tower of Shaker oval bentwood boxes in maple and cherry, drawn with devotional exactness on a cream laid-paper ground. Fine sepia pen traces every swallowtail joint, copper tack and growth ring. Flat transparent washes of milk-paint colours follow: buttermilk yellow, barn red and a soft chrome green. The composition is symmetrical and airy, with a peg rail across the top holding a single hanging chair. Rows of tidy ruled lines frame the stack and stand in for inscription. Nothing is shadowed dramatically; light is even and humble. It is meticulous and quiet, a gift of attention rather than spectacle.

A prize bull standing broadside at a county fair, its rosette pinned to the halter, with a young handler in pressed whites. The base is fine graphite tone in warm sepia, with hyperreal hide texture and every hair of the curly poll. Over it go thin, slightly mis-registered aniline tints: a rosy cheek, a pale turquoise sky, a dusty pink barn wall and a too-bright ribbon blue. The tints are watery and stop short of edges. The white border and soft vignette complete it. The mood is nostalgic, proud and faintly uncanny.

A frozen lake at mid-afternoon in deep winter, with a lone red ice-fishing shanty and an auger hole in the foreground. In the sky, a pale sun is flanked by two bright parhelia with faint red inner edges and a thin halo arc. These are laid in smooth sprayed gradients of cold cobalt to near white. The ice is hyperreal: pencil-drawn cracks, wind-scoured snow ripples and trapped bubbles. The horizon sits very low, and the vast sky dominates. It is bitterly bright, silent and enormous.

A hiker's elongated shadow is thrown onto a sea of cloud below a granite ridge, crowned by a concentric glory ring. The ring runs from soft red to amber, green and violet, laid in wet-in-wet watercolour bleeding into milky fog. The foreground rocks and boot-scuffed lichen are hyperreal and crisp, in sharp graphite and fine pen. The composition is vertiginous, seen from the ridge looking down and out, with the eerie figure centred far below. The palette is mostly pearl grey and blue-white. It is awe-struck and solitary.

A fat, salt-stiffened mooring rope knotted around an iron dock bollard, rendered entirely in drypoint-like line. Scratchy, burred black pen strokes bloom velvety at their edges where they cluster. Each frayed fibre and the rust pitting on the bollard is incised one stroke at a time. The paper is warm off-white, carrying a faint plate-tone smear of grey charcoal wiped unevenly across it. The marks are tight and nervous in the knot, dissolving to sparse scratches at the margins. It is a gritty, tactile monochrome study, intimate and slightly abrasive.

A trompe-l'oeil of a folded love letter lying on Victorian pierced paper lace. A crimson wax seal is cracked open, and a faded ribbon is tucked beneath. The lace is drawn in obsessive white-and-pale-grey pen filigree, with every punched hole, embossed rosette and paper-thickness shadow exact. It sits on a rose-madder ground. The handwriting on the envelope is suggested in iron-gall brown scribble. Soft gilt highlights catch the scalloped edges. It is ornate, sentimental and coy, meant to fool the eye into lifting the paper.

Seen from directly above, a dented baking tray is packed with cinnamon rolls. Every swirl is constructed like paper quilling, as tightly coiled ribbons of dough edged in fine brown pen. The layers are caramel, nutmeg and pale butter, given depth by graded watercolour washes on each strip's edge. Glossy sugar glaze drips across in translucent white, catching sharp specular highlights. Burnt sugar crusts in the corners and parchment paper buckles at the edges. The rhythm of repeating spirals is hypnotic but stays edible and photographic.

A strict grid of identical sugar cubes on a cool grey ground, evenly spaced and each lit from the same upper left. They are rendered in sharp graphite and white pencil, so every granular crystal and crumbling corner is exact. Each cube is very slightly different: a chipped edge, a lone ant, a faint tea stain migrating across the series. The light is flat and clinical, and the shadows are short and soft. It feels meditative and deadpan, the joy of noticing tiny deviations in sameness.

A pineapple seen straight down from above, its spiky crown cut away to show the interlocking spiral scales. Each eye is drawn with warty, hyperreal relief in sepia and burnt-umber ink hatching, and cross-hatched where it falls into shadow. Faint pencil construction lines overlay the fruit: counter-rotating spirals, a golden-angle protractor and tiny numbered annotations. These are like a diagram traced over a photograph. The paper is warm buff. It reads as part scientific plate, part trompe-l'oeil, and quietly obsessive.

A hotel doorman's half-length bust rendered with photographic exactness: braided epaulettes, stubble, a brass button reflecting the street. He is mirrored upside-down across a diagonal line, exactly like a king on a playing card. The image is built from dense, burnished coloured pencil in the card palette of vermilion, cobalt blue, egg-yolk yellow and jet black on a cream ground. Crisp black pen outlines frame the hyperreal modelling inside. A thin rounded-corner border encloses everything. It reads as formal and heraldic, yet uncannily real, a stranger turned into an emblem.

A tight, cropped portrait of a young woman's face seen through several sheets of bridal tulle at different distances. Each layer is a pale, transparent watercolour glaze in shell pink, oyster grey and faint champagne, overlapping into denser veils where the fabric folds. A hairline pen mesh of tiny hexagons lies over the skin, sharp on the nearest layer and blurred and doubled on the deeper ones. Behind all of it the eyes are rendered with ruthless pore-level precision in coloured pencil. The mood is hushed and breathy, a moiré of softness over clinical clarity.

Seen from overhead, a rumpled white linen bed fills the page diagonally. A greyhound sleeps curled in the creases, and a narrow prism rainbow from an unseen window falls across both the folds and the dog's flank. The linen and fur are carefully worked in soft graphite and white pencil, cool and nearly colourless. The spectrum stripe alone is wet-in-wet watercolour: cadmium red bleeding into lemon, viridian, ultramarine and violet. It bends over every ridge of fabric and every rib. The feeling is quiet and domestic, a single accidental miracle on an ordinary morning.

A worm's-eye view up into a carved plaster honeycomb ceiling, the stalactite cells cascading toward a central star. It is drawn in tonal charcoal on a warm mid-grey ground, with the shadows of each cell built from soft, blended mass. Raking afternoon light catches every chipped edge, and those highlights are lifted in crisp white chalk-pencil. Tiny lattice incisions and hairline cracks are picked out in hard graphite. There is no colour beyond faint sandstone warmth. The frame is filled edge to edge with intricate geometry, so the eye gets lost in a dizzying, hyper-detailed vault.

A frontal, edge-to-edge corkboard with no margins. Its warm honey-brown surface is built from thousands of tiny stippled pores and granules in coloured pencil, raw sienna and umber. Pinned across it are a faded bus ticket, a curling instant photo, a torn takeaway menu and a pressed receipt. Each one casts a soft shadow, and each sits on a coloured plastic pushpin rendered with glassy specular highlights. Every paper fibre, staple hole and crease is painstakingly exact. The mood is intimate and archival, a life inventoried at arm's length.

A top-down view into a matte black loudspeaker cone where coarse sea salt has jumped into nodal patterns: concentric rings, petals and crossing lines. The dark ground is dense charcoal mass with a soft rubbery sheen. Every salt grain is a stippled white or ice-grey point with a tiny cast shadow, crowded thick along the nodal lines and scattered thin elsewhere. The rim of the speaker's foam surround is rendered in exact pencil detail. The mood is austere and scientific, sound frozen into visible geometry.
